issue.title: Quota card: an unknown usage amount renders as a full allowance; a plugin span sent in ms is read as seconds, charting a window start at 2024-01-29
issue.body:
## Observed (live, 2026-10-24, provider `cloudflare-workers-ai` from `@magpie-community/opencode-cloudflare-workers-ai-auth` 0.0.3)

- The Workers AI account had consumed **10,756.27 of its 10,000/day free Neurons** (per Cloudflare's own GraphQL Analytics, `aiInferenceAdaptiveGroups.sum.totalNeurons`); every inference returned `429 / code 3036: you have used up your daily free allocation of 10000 neurons`.
- The provider's quota card nevertheless showed **`10,000 / 10,000 Neurons · 剩余 100%`**, freshly refreshed.
- `quota-history.json` on disk recorded: `\{"left": 100, "start": "2024-01-29T00:00:00Z", "resetsAt": "2026-10-25T00:00:00Z"\}` — the chart's x-axis rendered that start as 「1月29日 10:00」.
- The gateway had actually put the provider on rest for the rest of the day, so the card said the exact opposite of reality at the moment it mattered.

## Root cause A — an unknown amount is rendered as an untouched allowance

1. `internal/plugin/providers.go:1079`: `Amount float64 `json:"amount"`` — a plugin returning JSON `"amount": null` ("I don't know what was used") decodes silently to `0`. "Unknown" is unrepresentable in the type.
2. `internal/gui/assets/app.js:13937`: `const amount = Math.max(0, w.amount || 0), n = quotaLeft ? Math.max(0, w.limit - amount) : amount;` — `null || 0` again, so remaining = limit − 0 = 100% and the progress bar draws full.

Suggestion: `Amount *float64`, and when it is nil render 「已用 —」 with no filled bar (or show the window's `display` text) instead of a full allowance. Any plugin that reports a window without an amount currently misleads the same way.

## Root cause B — span unit mismatch (plugin fixed, but the card chart is where it shows)

The plugin sent `span: 86400000` (ms). `UsageWindow.span` is documented as **seconds** (`internal/plugin/providers.go:1082`), so `internal/provider/quota_history.go:189-192` (`Start = ResetsAt − span`) backed off **1,000 days**: 2026-10-25T00:00Z − 86,400,000 s = 2024-01-29T00:00Z — precisely the bogus axis start.

Plugin-side fix is in magpie-community/plugins#366 (sends `86400` now). Core-side, a defensive clamp would keep any future misbehaving plugin from charting a two-year window: e.g. treat `span` beyond `ResetsAt − now` (or > ~400 days) as invalid and fall back to the name-derived span.

## Environment

magpie `0.1.1364` (official image, Linux/docker).

comments.body:
Both root causes are fixed on `fix/issue-batch-1025a` ([d4944ace](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/d4944ace), skygunner's fork), my own filing from yesterday:

- **The span unit**: `windowSpan` now takes a vendor's span only up to 400 days — past every window a vendor runs it is a misread unit — and falls back to the name-derived span. Red first: your `span: 86400000` charted a "Daily" from **2024-01-29** (the exact date in the report); after, the name's 24h.
- **The unknown amount**: the host keeps `amount: null` null instead of collapsing it to 0, `QuotaWindow` carries `AmountUnknown` beside its limit (only when the vendor counts in amounts), and the count renders the vendor's own display text or `— / 10,000 Neurons` — never "10,000 / 10,000 · 100% left". Red first on the exact shape: `{"amount":null,"limit":10000}` read `Count(left) = "10,000 / 10,000 Neurons"`.

Tests: `TestQuotaHistoryMillisecondSpan` (the reporter's JSON), the fake plugin's fourth window (amount null, limit 10000) end-to-end through the host, and a new Playwright test (`quota-amount-unknown.test.cjs`, Chromium + WebKit, en + zh) that showed "10,000 / 10,000 Neurons · 剩余 100%" before the fix — the card as you saw it. `go test ./internal/provider ./internal/plugin` green (except the known local #2207), quota-credits/quota-count-wrap unchanged.

One honest note: the plugin-side fix (magpie-community/plugins#366 sending seconds) remains the real cure; the core changes are the defense that keeps the next misbehaving plugin honest.

Reporter follow-up: the Cloudflare plugin fixes are now deployed and confirmed working, and have been pushed to [magpie-community/plugins#366](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins/pull/366) at [bdc302a](https://github.com/skygunner/plugins/commit/bdc302a6d66187d20d923673a61dd26ce13513a5).

The remaining permission hint was caused by two plugin integration bugs: an aggregate ordered by an unselected `datetimeHour` (a GraphQL syntax error), and reading `result.viewer` instead of Cloudflare's actual `data.viewer` response. The same saved token now returns the real daily usage. Known readings also carry their percentage and use the standard numeric count, so Used / Left is clickable and the used amount is no longer clipped inside a long display sentence. Paid/unknown plans mark the free allowance `aside: true`, preserving routing beyond the included allowance.

Confirmed on the deployed card: 23,821.83 / 10,000 Neurons used, or 0 / 10,000 left, with a 24-hour window. Node tests 23/23; full plugin-repository Bun suite 2465/2465; Chromium/WebKit checks in English/Chinese at 420/1100px pass. The core null-amount/span handling described earlier and this plugin PR remain separate changes; this update reports the working plugin path.

Integration follow-up for **v0.1.1767 + our carried patches**: [b6f71ebd](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/b6f71ebd8e7824148fc658347ba0561505deb15e) on [`fix/3487-quota-span-fixture-1767`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3487-quota-span-fixture-1767) updates the newer `TestQuotaSpanCarriesEveryWindowField` fixture to set `AmountUnknown: true`.

The all-fields guard failed because its fixture did not set the field added by our #3487 patch; `quotaReport` already copies the field correctly. This is a **one-line test integration repair, with no runtime behavior change**. The quota and plugin-usage checks pass 20 repetitions under race detection; native/Linux/Windows vet pass. It is pushed for cherry-picking by our deployment integrator, not deployed by this work.

We also checked whether #3487 or plugins#366 caused Hindsight's non-streaming 200/missing-choices symptom. The reproduced cause is instead the independent timeout patch described in [#3788's corrected implementation note](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3788#issuecomment-6432514407): a non-streaming wait accidentally sent SSE keepalives. The quota/plugin fixes do not enable that path.

comments.body: Integration follow-up for **v0.1.1948 + our carried patches**: upstream's 1390aa458 (community plugins#468) takes this issue's point over its own way — a plugin window's `amount` is a bare count again, where 0 is what a count left out reads as, and a limit alone says nothing (`quotaOfPlugin` leaves such a window as text/aside). The carried pointer form (`d4944ace`'s `amountUnknown` flag) cannot sit beside that type change, so our `prod` integration now carries only what upstream lacks: the quota card and tray still refuse to draw a full allowance for a limit with no count (vendor's words or `— / 10,000`, never `10,000 / 10,000`), and the millisecond-span guard (`quotaSpanLimit`) stays. The fake plugin's `Daily` window (`amount: null`) stays as the pipeline regression.

issue.title: cloudflare-workers-ai 0.0.4: read actual Neurons and restore quota-card toggles

repository.name: plugins
repository.description: Community-maintained OpenCode provider plugins for coding-plan subscriptions (work in OpenCode and magpie)

issue.body:
## Problem

Workers AI's quota hook reports an unknown amount and sends its daily span in milliseconds. The account can exhaust its free allowance while the card looks untouched, and the quota chart derives a start date about 1,000 days too early.

The GraphQL integration also needs the actual Cloudflare response shape and a valid aggregate query. Sorting by an unselected `datetimeHour` returns HTTP 200 with a GraphQL syntax error; reading `result.viewer` misses the successful response's `data.viewer`. Both failures leave the card showing an Analytics-permission hint even when the token has access.

## Resulting behavior

- Query today's UTC interval through GraphQL Analytics, sum `aiInferenceAdaptiveGroups.sum.totalNeurons`, and read `data.viewer.accounts`. The aggregate query needs no ordering.
- Report the real `amount`, `limit: 10000`, `unit`, daily `span: 86400`, and next UTC midnight as `resetsAt`. An empty day is zero; failed or unavailable readings remain unknown.
- For a known amount, report its capped `used` percentage and leave `display` empty. Magpie then uses its standard numeric count and clickable Used / Left control, avoiding the long clipped sentence.
- Set `aside: true` for Paid or unconfirmed plans. Their included free allowance is visible but excluded from routing limits. Only a confirmed Free plan makes this window a hard cap.
- When an inference actually receives HTTP 429 with code 3036, preserve its response body and add `Retry-After` until the next UTC midnight. Other 429 responses retain their own retry behavior.
- Update English, Simplified Chinese and Japanese documentation for Analytics permissions, the daily allowance, reset time, and informational windows.

The daily free allowance is 10,000 Neurons for both Free and Paid plans; Paid usage can continue beyond it. [Cloudflare pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/pricing/).

## Verification

At `bdc302a`:

- `node --check packages/cloudflare-workers-ai/src/index.mjs`
- `node --test packages/cloudflare-workers-ai/test/plugin.test.mjs`: **23 passed**
- `bun scripts/check.mjs cloudflare-workers-ai`: passed
- Full repository `bun test` under a temporary HOME: **2465 passed, 0 failed, 213 files**
- `git diff --check`: passed

Regression checks fail when independently restoring the wrong GraphQL envelope, invalid aggregate ordering, enforcing Paid/unknown allowances, or omitting unknown-plan percentages.

Live verification with the same saved token: the old query returns the sorting error; the corrected query returns **23,821.8265 Neurons**. The deployed plugin's quota API now reports `used: 100` with that amount and no text-only marker. Chromium and WebKit checks using that API response, in English/Chinese at 420/1100px, confirm the card toggles between **23,821.83 / 10,000 used** and **0 / 10,000 left** without clipping. The reporter confirmed the deployed fixes work.

Not tested: a real Workers Paid account's billing or continued paid inference; its routing protection is covered by the Paid and unknown-plan regressions. Version remains **0.0.4**; upstream main is at 0.0.3, and npm currently returns E404 for the package.

Related core handling: https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3487.

issue.title: Feature request: support non-streaming requests in the group FirstToken timeout

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Request

Please consider applying the existing routing group's `FirstToken` timeout to **non-streaming requests (`stream:false`)** as well.

This would let a group switch to its next candidate when a non-streaming upstream stalls before producing response content, just as it can for a streaming request. It need not introduce a new setting or change the cancellation/cooldown policy.

## Concrete use case

Hindsight sends non-streaming Chat Completions requests. If a candidate stalls, the existing `FirstToken` setting does not advance to the next candidate; the caller can reach its own HTTP timeout and disconnect before the gateway gives the fallback a chance.

In the v0.1.1612-based code we investigated, the gateway sets the first-content timer only when `streams` is true:

```go
if isGroup && firstToken > 0 && !last && streams {
    hw.firstWait = time.Duration(firstToken) * time.Second
}
```

There is a second relevant detail: receiving JSON response headers marks the reply as `whole`, which the existing `holdWriter.started()` treats as started even if no body content has arrived. Extending the timer must also handle this header-only stall.

## Expected behavior

- Reuse the group's existing `FirstToken` duration for `stream:false`.
- If the upstream has supplied no response-body content within that duration, cancel that attempt and try the next candidate while the caller is still connected.
- Headers alone must not satisfy the first-content deadline.
- Preserve existing semantics: zero disables the budget, a final candidate is not interrupted by this fallback budget, and a reply already started is not cut off by it.

For a fully buffered non-streaming upstream, the gateway cannot observe the model's actual first generated token. The measurable equivalent is **first response-body content / time to response**, not internal generation TTFT. This request is about that fallback deadline, not an overall completion timeout.

## Reproduction and local check

Our regression serves two candidates: the first immediately sends JSON headers and then stalls; the second returns a valid JSON completion. With a one-second group budget and a three-second caller deadline, the original code reaches the caller deadline instead of returning the fallback. With the timeout applied to non-streaming first content, the second candidate answers after approximately one second.

The regression, repeated targeted race tests, and an isolated compiled-binary HTTP smoke test pass. Our local fork is deployed, and a non-streaming production request using Hindsight's caller credential also returned successfully; that production smoke check does not by itself establish a long-term latency improvement.

Reference implementation:
https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/dd670e6e67cdc4535917d9aa8bb2130abbf88e43

That local commit contains both this change and a separate optional cancellation-cooldown experiment, now tracked in #3791. **This issue asks only for the non-streaming timeout extension**; the two features can be reviewed and accepted independently, and any PR for this issue should isolate the timeout changes.

The full Go suite has unrelated failures reproduced on our unchanged production baseline; the local patch does not claim a green full suite.

Would this extension of `FirstToken` fit the intended routing behavior?

Integration follow-up for **v0.1.1767 + our carried patches**: [b6f71ebd](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/b6f71ebd8e7824148fc658347ba0561505deb15e) on [`fix/3487-quota-span-fixture-1767`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3487-quota-span-fixture-1767) updates the newer `TestQuotaSpanCarriesEveryWindowField` fixture to set `AmountUnknown: true`.

The all-fields guard failed because its fixture did not set the field added by our #3487 patch; `quotaReport` already copies the field correctly. This is a **one-line test integration repair, with no runtime behavior change**. The quota and plugin-usage checks pass 20 repetitions under race detection; native/Linux/Windows vet pass. It is pushed for cherry-picking by our deployment integrator, not deployed by this work.

We also checked whether #3487 or plugins#366 caused Hindsight's non-streaming 200/missing-choices symptom. The reproduced cause is instead the independent timeout patch described in [#3788's corrected implementation note](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3788#issuecomment-6432514407): a non-streaming wait accidentally sent SSE keepalives.
